transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood Solutions), Carlos (Crestwave Head of ML), Sana (Crestwave Platform), Tom (Crestwave VP Product), Leah (SRE)

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for squeezing this in, we'll do a quick 40 minute standup on the bench results vs the incumbent and then triage the tail spikes, um hi Carlos, hi Sana, thanks for joining.
00:22 Carlos: hey thanks Jordan, excited to see the numbers, we got the earlier summary email but want to dig into the tail behavior — that's our main risk.
00:35 Priya: cool quick agenda: 1) short recap of runs we did this week, 2) median/95/99 numbers vs LegacyServe, 3) hypotheses for spikes, 4) repro plan and next steps. Sound ok?
00:50 Tom: yep sounds good. Also can we cover any security asks briefly? We have the SSO question.
01:02 Jordan: sure we'll hit security at the end. Alright Priya take us through the runs.
01:10 Priya: thanks — so we ran three batches: steady QPS 40, burst QPS peak 220 for 30s, and mixed daytime traffic from your trace that Sana provided. The models used were redwood-v0.9.f32 (non-quant) and a 4-bit quant variant as a fallback. Results: median token latency for redwood-v0.9 was 28ms vs LegacyServe 45ms under steady load; under burst median was 35ms vs 62ms. However 99.9th percentile hit 1.2s in two of the burst runs on our side, and LegacyServe showed a more consistent 400-500ms tail.
02:02 Carlos: ok so median is great, tail is worse in some cases, can you show the timeline for the spike?
02:10 Priya: yeah slide 3 in the deck — the spike correlates with a cache miss window after a route chop — basically the KV cache wasn't warmed for some prefix patterns and batching fell back to single-request paths. Also we saw an increased CPU steal on the worker during those seconds which made the spike worse.
02:42 Leah: when you say KV cache, is that the prefix cache in the runtime? We call it kay-vee in our notes sometimes lol.
02:49 Priya: yes the prefix/KV cache — apologies for different terms. The runtime does prefix caching and also keeps a per-route small LRU for recently used keys. When a burst with new prefixes hits, initial requests pay cache load plus kernel JIT paths and that can add 300-600ms.
03:11 Sana: are you using continuous batching? I thought that would smooth tails.
03:18 Priya: we do, but continuous batching has a timeout heuristic. If traffic has immediate spikes with many unique prefixes, the batcher will create more mini-batches to avoid waiting which increases per-token overhead. We tuned the batcher to favor latency but that increases throughput cost.
03:38 Evan: also note we saw a misconfigured autoscaler flag in one run where the burst nodes weren't added fast enough — that was a human config miss on our end earlier this week, not representative.
03:51 Jordan: important callout — that autoscaler hiccup explains some of the worst tail numbers; we repeated the run after fixing and the 99.9th dropped to ~650ms.
04:03 Carlos: ok that's helpful. But LegacyServe's tail was 400-500 consistently — what's left to close that gap?
04:12 Priya: three things: 1) prefix warmup via synthetic priming (we can seed common prefixes), 2) adjust batcher timeout and size for your QPS shape, 3) small model-variant fallback quicker on tail detection (we tested 4-bit variant, but switching earlier helps). Combined we estimate tail median improvement to ~450ms.
04:40 Tom: what's the cost impact of switching earlier to the quantized fallback?
04:45 Priya: approximate unit cost goes down 18-25% for tokens served on quant variant, but quality delta — for your usage we saw negligible drift on short summarization prompts, we will share the eval diffs.
05:02 Sana: can you share the exact queries where you saw quality drift? We need to validate with our product team.
05:08 Priya: yes will attach sample queries and the opposite examples where the quant variant trimmed a token or two.
05:17 Jordan: quick interjection — one interesting find: LegacyServe had a higher pre-warm hit rate because they pin a small warm cache per tenant, which costs them reserved memory; we can mimic that with a small reserved pin for high-traffic routes. That reduces tail but increases memory footprint ~6-8%.
05:40 Carlos: memory ok, budget is fine as long as SLA holds during office hours.
05:45 Leah: what about network egress and cross-region hits? Some spikes in our trace were from cross-region fallbacks.
05:52 Priya: good catch — we saw a handful of tail events when failover routed to a different AZ. That added 70-120ms. If you want stricter regional routing we can pin routes, albeit with less failover flexibility.
06:10 Tom: we'd prefer pinning for priority routes. Non-critical routes can keep flexible failover.
06:18 Jordan: noted — we'll provide a routing policy suggestion doc.
06:23 Priya: back to repro plan — proposal: 4-hour dedicated slot next Friday (2026-10-22) where we run a deterministic tail harness with your weekend-like spike pattern, we'll seed prefixes and toggle batcher timeout. We'll capture raw logs and request IDs to correlate with your traces.
06:43 Carlos: Friday works for us. One ask: can you enable verbose sampling for 1% of requests so we can inspect KV cache decisions?
06:51 Priya: yes we can do that, cost is minimal. We'll redact any PII.
06:55 Sana: security — we need a quick SSO/SAML checklist for the Private deployment. Also audit log retention questions.
07:03 Jordan: short answer: we support SSO via SAML 2.0, RBAC with SCIM groups, and audit logs retained 90 days by default — enterprise packages can extend. We'll push the security packet and an architecture note for VPC/private deployment.
07:18 Tom: will you include KMS options for key management? We need HSM-level assurances for some workloads.
07:24 Evan: yes we support customer-managed KMS in Private with HSM-backed options; we'll add the specifics to the security doc.
07:31 Carlos: back to the numbers — can you walk through the CSV columns you will share? Need to map to our telemetry fields.
07:40 Jordan: the CSV will include timestamp, request_id, route, prefix_hash, model_variant, batch_size, latency_ms (token and request), node_id, worker_cpu, cache_hit boolean, and any autoscaler event markers.
07:56 Leah: include az/region tag please.
07:58 Jordan: will do.
08:01 Priya: small note about metrics: our median token latency is measured at token emit time; some systems measure request end-to-end differently — we will include measurement mapping so you can compare apples-to-apples with LegacyServe numbers.
08:18 Carlos: important. Also how reproducible is the 99.9th improvement after your fixes?
08:24 Priya: after the autoscaler fix and a 10s batcher tweak we got 99.9th ~650ms in local runs. With pinned warm cache and earlier fallback to quantized variant we predict ~430-500ms. We'll validate in the dedicated slot.
08:40 Tom: what do you need from us to start the dedicated slot?
08:45 Priya: final QPS pattern (tps per route) for the run, confirmation of which routes to pin, and access to the small eval dataset. Sana will provide QPS patterns.
08:54 Sana: I'll send the QPS file by EOD tomorrow.
08:58 Jordan: perfect. Any blockers on rollout?
09:02 Carlos: only security signoff and a short PR for cost impact. We need estimated incremental monthly cost if we reserve the warm cache and enable higher memory.
09:12 Priya: we'll put an estimate in the benchmark spreadsheet.
09:16 Jordan: recap quick: 1) Jordan: share full CSV + perf histograms by 2026-10-21, 2) Priya: provision dedicated slot run 2026-10-22 and run tail-latency harness, 3) Sana: QPS pattern + sample queries 2026-10-21, 4) Redwood send security packet + KMS/HSM note by 2026-10-23.
09:39 Carlos: thanks everyone. One last thing — can you include a short note on how your fallback policy decides when to route to quantized variant? We call it the 'fallthrough' logic.
09:49 Priya: yes we'll add a one-pager. It uses token-rate and moving-window tail percentiles per route, currently thresholded at observed 95p > X ms. We'll show the tuning knobs.
10:02 Tom: great thanks. If we see improvement in the dedicated run, next step is a week-long pilot with daylight traffic.
10:10 Jordan: sounds like a plan. We'll follow up with an invite for the dedicated slot and attach the CSV. Thanks all.
10:20 (call ends)
notes: Benchmarked redwood-v0.9 non-quant and 4-bit fallback; autoscaler misconfig contributed to worst tails; plan dedicated slot and seed prefixes; security docs and SAML/KMS follow-up; cost estimate for pinned warm cache requested.
